method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; reviewed complete plaintext source, cleave facts including literals/flow and atomscan before/after. Isolated Python execution used stubbed imports, network, archives, process launch, deletion and Windows APIs; no sample operation executed on the host.
source_scope: The primary incident report independently documents the exact staging URL, Radmin path, FamItrfc.exe --runtimechk task action, three-hour interval and mutex. It establishes campaign association; these scripts are not the published native CROSSROAD executable, and their provenance is unknown.
common_execution: Downloads https://promotion.storage-data.com/config/component.zip to TEMP/component.zip without an integrity check.
Extracts the fetched ZIP to LOCALAPPDATA/Radmin. PowerShell uses -Force.
Builds a FamItrfc.exe --runtimechk action and invokes schtasks /create /sc hourly /mo 3 /tr ... /f. This registers future activation; no immediate payload launch or /run is present.
Deletes its own source path after task registration. This does not delete the staged archive or payload.
verdict_basis: MALICIOUS for all three: reachable acquisition from the published SHINYROAD delivery URL linked to the published persistent payload path/action and loader cleanup. The exact campaign configuration tips the balance beyond ordinary maintenance installation; names or ML scores alone were not used to convict.
not_established: No original package, signer, legitimate deployment authorization, or author provenance is supplied.
The fetched archive could not be retrieved (DNS failure), so its current bytes, archive members, payload integrity and runtime effects are unknown.

Do not attribute the downstream backdoor DLL, sideloading, credential theft, spying, C2 command dispatch, privilege escalation, geofencing or ADS self-deletion to these scripts. Those operations do not appear in their source.
No obfuscation, decoded executable layer or hidden code was found; literals and control flow are plaintext.

distinct_paths.argv_task_loader.py: Creates a global mutex through ctypes, exits when GetLastError()==183, otherwise stages the archive, registers ComponentRuntime with a list argv and deletes itself. Any exception stops later steps. The unquoted executable inside /TR can be ambiguous for paths containing spaces.
distinct_paths.archive_task_loader.py: No mutex. Passes a single command-line string to subprocess.run, which is a Windows CreateProcess invocation, not shell=True. Download/extraction failure or check=True task failure prevents self-deletion.
distinct_paths.archive_task_loader.ps1: No mutex or terminating-error policy. Depending on cmdlet error severity it can continue after failures; a schtasks nonzero exit does not itself prevent Remove-Item. The constructed /TR action quotes the executable path.

severity_and_placement_corrections.unsupported_claim: AppData path construction adds no hostile admission to a self-deleting repeating-task installer, and does not establish C2 or immediate execution.
severity_and_placement_corrections.counterexample: The inert digest-verified maintenance-setup.py control fires the old hostile rule when scanned outside a testing directory. The relocated observation retains its matcher, confidence, exclusions and behavioral mappings.

severity_and_placement_corrections.unsupported_claim: A variable /TR action plus Join-Path of an executable adds no malicious intent to the existing suspicious installer behavior. The composite does not prove variable flow.
severity_and_placement_corrections.counterexample: The inert digest-verified maintenance-setup.ps1 control fires this rule at hostile severity before the edit, suspicious after.

severity_and_placement_corrections.correction: Description now says config or feature-flag path segment: the unchanged matcher accepts /config/component.zip, not only URLs ending at config.

new_detection.evidence: Parsed, qualified ctypes.windll.kernel32.CreateMutex[AW] call. API text, a local function declaration and same-name variable are negative controls. Native CreateMutex rules and their consumers are unchanged.

consumer_audit: Exact moved-ID search found no consumers. Audited every ancestor selector: three FTP banner consumers, the hosts-sinkhole consumer and CrystalX exclusion. Each explicitly retains the moved observation, preserving its former selector population. New mutex atom has no ancestor selector consumers and leaves native API scope unchanged.
coverage_requirement: All samples retain two distinct supported suspicious behaviors across evasion/self-delete and persistence/system/scheduled-task. The argv variant also retains its family-specific hostile association. The generic installation mechanics do not justify inventing additional hostile traits.

tests.boundary_controls: 4 archive-task and mutex controls passed outside test-directory suppressors. Both ordinary installers lose unsupported hostile severity while all supported suspicious behaviors remain.
tests.python_mock_execution: 10 isolated traces passed: success, existing-mutex, download failure, extraction failure, task failure for each Python source. The no-mutex variant ignores the simulated existing mutex state as expected.
tests.outside_batch_coverage: 149 preexisting findings across task-stub.c, clickfix-update-stager.ps1, ps-cradle-stager.ps1 and setup-verified-library-download/setup.py were identical before and after the shared-rule edits. This preserves their current attack/capability coverage; it is not a claim that existing coverage is complete.

analysis_limits: Cleave records flow-query-incomplete for the Python sources; direct source tracing and stubbed execution resolve the relevant paths independently. Atomscan warns that its v18 models consume a newer v19 feature schema. Both limitations are retained in the scan evidence.
